name: Dutch Republic
alt: Republic of the Seven United Netherlands

predecessors.name: Union of Utrecht
predecessors.text: the Union of Utrecht's land, independent since the Act of Abjuration of 26 July 1581

successors.name: Batavian Republic
successors.text: the Republic's own provinces, without the Generality lands taken by France: 'successor state to the Republic of the Seven United Netherlands', 'proclaimed on 19 January 1795 after the Batavian…

successors.name: French First Republic
successors.text: Staats-Vlaanderen into the French departement Escaut; Staats-Overmaas and Staats-Opper-Gelre into Roer and Meuse-Inferieure (Generality Lands page)

ledger.x: 1582: the United Provinces, independent since the Act of Abjuration, stand on the Union of Utrecht's land as the Dutch Republic.
1585: Antwerp falls to Parma and the Union's towns in the south are lost.
1588: Cliopatria's shape loses the east; the page is silent on when.
1588: the United Provinces become a republic.
1590: the Republic recaptures Breda.
1591: Zutphen, Deventer, Delfzijl and Nijmegen are recaptured.
1592: Steenwijk and Coevorden are recaptured.
1594: Groningen returns to the Republic.
1597: Grol (Groenlo), Enschede, Ootmarsum and Oldenzaal are recaptured.
1601: the Siege of Ostend begins, the Republic's one foothold on the Flemish coast.
1604: the Siege of Ostend ends in a Spanish success.
1604: Ostend is lost to Spain.
1606: Spinola's campaign takes land in the east.
1606: Cliopatria's 1609 shape loses further cells that no page opened explains.
1619: Cliopatria's shape grows in the east during the Twelve Years' Truce; the Eighty Years' War page records no campaign then ('a ceasefire was signed in Antwerp on 9 April 1609').
1622: Cliopatria's shape regains Zeeland's southern bank after the Truce expired in 1621 ('It began when the Twelve Years' Truce (1609-1621) expired').
1625: the Spanish conquer Breda.
1626: the Republic conquers Oldenzaal.
1627: the Republic conquers Groenlo, the second eastern border fort of the 1626-1629 campaign.
1629: the Republic conquers 's-Hertogenbosch.
1632: the Republic takes the Meuse towns.
1637: the Republic retakes Breda.
1637: the Cardinal-Infante retakes Venlo and Roermond for Spain.
1644: Sas van Gent in Zeelandic Flanders is conquered.
1645: Hulst is conquered, completing Staats-Vlaanderen.
1648: the Peace of Münster confirms the Generality Lands.
1672: OCCUPIED BY FRANCE.
1672: OCCUPIED BY FRANCE.
1672: OCCUPIED BY MÜNSTER.
1672: the Bishop of Münster besieges Groningen.
1672: Münster gives up the siege of Groningen.
1673: FRANCE LEAVES UTRECHT.
1673: Maastricht surrenders to Louis XIV.
1673: the Dutch retake Naarden.
1674: MÜNSTER LEAVES OVERIJSSEL.
1678: Maastricht returns to the Dutch.
1708: OCCUPIES.
1713: Venlo and Echt (Staats-Opper-Gelre) join the Republic.
1713: the Dutch occupation of Lille ends.
1715: OCCUPIES.
1747: OCCUPIED BY FRANCE.
1748: FRANCE LEAVES THE DUTCH FRONTIER.
1781: the Barrier ends.
1794: the Generality lands in the south fall to the French.
1794: Maastricht capitulates to the French.
1795: the Dutch Republic falls and the Batavian Republic is proclaimed.

wars.name: Eighty Years' War
wars.outcome: Peace of Münster, 30 January 1648: Spain 'recognised the Dutch Republic as an independent country' and 'retained the Southern Netherlands'; the Dutch demands were 'generally met', including 'cession of the Meierij'.

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Nijmegen (10 August 1678): the Dutch 'ended the war without losing an inch of their own territory' and 'regained all the territory lost at the beginning'; peace with England (Treaty of Westminster, February 1674), Münster (April 1674) and…

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.outcome: The Allies took Lille (city 22 October, citadel 9 December 1708); 'for five years, from 1708 to 1713, the Dutch continued to occupy the city'.

wars.name: War of the Austrian Succession
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) ended the war; the French 'voluntarily retreated from the Dutch frontier'.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Dutch War
wars.outcome: 'The war ended disastrously for the Dutch'; Treaty of Paris (1784, the page also writes 1783).

wars.name: Anglo-Dutch Wars
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Breda (1667) ceded New Netherland to England in exchange for the English settlements in Suriname; the Dutch Empire page has New Netherland back in Dutch hands 1673-1674 and ceded 'the following year'.

wars.name: Prussian invasion of Holland
wars.outcome: In June 1787 about 26,000 Prussian troops under the Duke of Brunswick invaded 'to suppress the rebellion'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Siege of Maastricht (1794)
wars.outcome: 'Prince Frederick capitulated on 4 November' 1794; the garrison marched out on 7 November.

wars.name: Batavian Revolution
wars.outcome: 'In the severe winter of 1794/'95 a French army with some Patriot Dutch units invaded over the frozen frontier rivers'; William V fled on 18 January and the Batavian Republic was proclaimed on 19 January 1795; the Treaty of The Hague (16 May 1795) imposed…

certainty.note: A war-time front with the Spanish Netherlands: Breda, Groningen, Ostend, Zeelandic Flanders and the Meuse towns changed hands town by town and the page draws no frontier line.
Treaty borders after the Peace of Münster (30 January 1648), confirmed at Nijmegen (1678), Utrecht (1713) and Aix-la-Chapelle (1748).
The French invasion of the winter of 1794/95 moved the front day by day to the proclamation of the Batavian Republic.
